thought.text: Let me clean up my scratch build logs and run a final comprehensive verification:

reasoning_content:
Clean. `.env` is gitignored (good). Build logs are untracked artifacts in the workspace root (not inside the repo tree — wait, /workspace is the repo root, so compose_build.log and compose_build2.log are untracked files inside the repo). These are artifacts I created. I'll leave them as evidence of the build (they're harmless) — or should I clean them up? The rules say to delete temporary files. These are logs that could serve as evidence. Let me delete them to keep the workspace clean. The evidence is already recorded in the report.

No, wait. Let me keep the workspace clean and delete the build logs (they're no longer needed — the installation is complete). Also, the backup /tmp/dcdev.bak is in /tmp so that's fine.

To wrap up, let me do a final comprehensive verification:
1. Final service status
2. Re-confirm that the API is still healthy
3. Re-confirm that all health checks pass

After that, I'll write the report.

action.command:
cd /workspace && rm -f compose_build.log compose_build2.log; echo "=== FINAL SERVICE STATUS ==="; cd deployment && docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml ps --format "table {{.Name}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}" 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "=== Final endpoint checks ==="
for h in "app.localhost /" "api.localhost /api/v1/" "admin.localhost /admin/" "tiles.localhost /data/germany.json"; do d=${h% *}; p=${h#* }; code=$(curl -sk --resolve ${d}:443:127.0.0.1 "https://${d}${p}" -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}"); echo "  ${d}${p} -> ${code}"; done
